items.target_frame: amae: expected relational indulgence within intimate hierarchy
items.explanation: English 'dependence' is often pathologized. Amae names a culturally legible plea for indulgent care—not mere inability.
items.evidence: Doi, Takeo. The Anatomy of Dependence (Amae no Kōzō).

items.target_frame: wa: prioritized group concord shaping speech and self-presentation
items.explanation: English 'harmony' is aesthetic/social calm. Wa is a normative social good that can license indirectness and self-restraint.
items.evidence: Lebra, Takie. Japanese Patterns of Behavior; discussions of wa in intercultural pragmatics.

items.target_frame: structured dual stance: honne (inner) / tatemae (official front)
items.explanation: Honne/tatemae is an institutionalized dual presentation, not just 'white lies' versus honesty.
items.evidence: Lebra; intercultural communication texts on honne and tatemae.

items.target_frame: kuuki: normative atmosphere one must 'read' (空気を読む)
items.explanation: Kuuki o yomu makes atmosphere a readable social demand; English 'vibe' is lighter and less obligatory.
items.evidence: Yamamoto Shichihei on 'air'; contemporary discussions of 空気を読む.

items.target_frame: natsukashii: warm recognition of something personally familiar from before
items.explanation: Natsukashii is often triggered by sensory recognition of the familiar past—closer to fond familiarity than melancholic nostalgia alone.
items.evidence: Japanese emotion vocabulary studies; bilingual dictionary contrast notes.

items.target_frame: ritual acknowledgment of shared labor and reciprocal fatigue
items.explanation: Otsukaresama is phatic workplace ritual recognizing mutual exertion; English thanks-for-your-work is thinner socially.
items.evidence: Japanese business communication manuals; pragmatic studies of お疲れ様です.

items.target_frame: enryo: institutionalized non-imposition and self-restraint
items.explanation: Enryo is socially expected restraint against imposing; English 'you're too polite' mishears it as mere shyness.
items.evidence: Lebra on enryo; Japanese politeness research.

items.target_frame: majime: reliable earnestness valued as character
items.explanation: Majime praises conscientious reliability, not only 'not funny' seriousness.
items.evidence: Japanese character-term discussions; bilingual learner dictionaries.

items.target_frame: gaman: virtuous endurance of hardship without complaint
items.explanation: Gaman moralizes enduring; English 'patience' can be thinner and less characterological.
items.evidence: Cultural psychology notes on gaman; Japanese values literature.

items.target_frame: ikigai: worth-of-living nested in daily roles, not only grand passion
items.explanation: Popular English 'ikigai' charts oversimplify; the Japanese term centers worth in living, including mundane roles.
items.evidence: Kamiya Mieko on ikigai; critiques of Westernized ikigai diagrams.

items.target_frame: single lexical package for light leaking through leaves
items.explanation: Komorebi is a ready-made aesthetic lexical item; English needs a descriptive phrase.
items.evidence: Japanese aesthetic vocabulary lists; bilingual 'untranslatable' compilations.

items.target_frame: shibui: astringent, refined restraint in taste
items.explanation: Shibui names an aesthetic of restrained refinement; English 'understated' lacks the astringent taste metaphor.
items.evidence: Aesthetic vocabulary in Japanese art history; Keene and related discussions.

items.target_frame: ritual humble receiving before eating
items.explanation: Itadakimasu is a set ritual formula of receiving; English meal thanks vary and lack the fixed humble verb.
items.evidence: Japanese formula routines in pragmatics textbooks.

items.target_frame: mottainai: regret that value/potential is not fully used
items.explanation: Mottainai blends waste regret with respect for inherent value—broader than 'don't waste that'.
items.evidence: Popularized globally via environmental campaigns; Japanese usage notes.

items.target_frame: sempai–kōhai: enduring hierarchical role pair with duties
items.explanation: Sempai/kōhai is a durable institutional relation, not only 'senior at work'.
items.evidence: Rohlen and educational ethnographies; Japanese organizational culture texts.

items.target_frame: kaizen: shop-floor continuous improvement ethos
items.explanation: As English management jargon, kaizen is thinner than Japanese workplace-improvement practice histories.
items.evidence: Imai Masaaki; lean/TPS historical overviews.

items.target_frame: omotenashi: anticipatory hospitality without expectation of tip-like return
items.explanation: Omotenashi emphasizes anticipatory care; English 'hospitality' is broader and commercially flatter.
items.evidence: Tourism discourse analyses of omotenashi; Japanese service culture writing.

items.target_frame: shōganai: socially routine acceptance of uncontrollable circumstance
items.explanation: Shōganai is an everyday acceptance formula; English 'it is what it is' is close but less ritualized.
items.evidence: Japanese conversational routines; intercultural communication notes.

items.target_frame: ganbaru: culturally saturated perseverance ethos
items.explanation: Ganbaru is ubiquitous encouragement/identity talk about persevering; English 'do your best' is weaker as a social script.
items.evidence: Cultural discussions of ganbaru in education and sports.

items.target_frame: uchi/soto: pervasive in-out boundary shaping language and obligation
items.explanation: Uchi/soto organizes linguistic and social boundaries more systematically than casual English in-group talk.
items.evidence: Lebra; Bachnik & Quinn (eds.) Situated Meaning on uchi/soto.

items.target_frame: nemawashi: root-binding informal consensus before formal decision
items.explanation: Nemawashi is expected organizational practice; English 'lobbying' can sound adversarial.
items.evidence: Japanese management literature on nemawashi.

items.target_frame: wabi-sabi: aesthetic of transience and humble imperfection
items.explanation: Wabi-sabi is a dense aesthetic complex; English 'imperfect beauty' is a thin calque.
items.evidence: Japanese aesthetics overviews (e.g. Juniper; classic tea-culture sources).

items.target_frame: jiyū: freedom with distinct modern-Japanese political history
items.explanation: Jiyū translates freedom/liberty but sits in Meiji-to-present political vocabulary with different emphases than Anglo-American liberty talk.
items.evidence: Intellectual histories of 自由 in modern Japan.

items.target_frame: en: karmic/fateful human connection
items.explanation: En names relational fate; English 'connection' is transactional or vague by comparison.
items.evidence: Buddhist-influenced Japanese relational vocabulary notes.

items.target_frame: kawaii: expansive aesthetic/social category beyond childlike cute
items.explanation: Kawaii saturates aesthetics and social evaluation more widely than English 'cute'.
items.evidence: Yomota Inuhiko; cultural studies of kawaii.
